chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all together, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me and to Suleiman ibn Khalid: 'I have prohibited the Mut'ah for the two of you from myself as long as you both are in Medina, because you two frequently come to me, so I fear that you would be seized, and it would be said, 'These are the companions of Ja'far.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq prohibit Mut'ah for specific companions in Medina?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a specific, temporary prohibition of Mut'ah for Sahl ibn Ziyad and Suleiman ibn Khalid while they resided in Medina, distinguishing this from a general abrogation of the practice. This ruling was a pragmatic political precaution (tadabbur) to prevent the companions from being arrested alongside the Imam, which could have led the public to conflate their status with his, thereby complicating the political landscape during periods of Umayyad surveillance.
